# nullable-boolean

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

A nullable boolean has three states: true, false and NULL. Code reads it as two, so NULL silently behaves as false in some places and as an error in others, and queries like WHERE flag = false skip the NULL rows.

## Fix

Make the field non-nullable in the model, give it a default, and backfill existing NULL rows before regenerating the schema. If a third state is real, model it explicitly, for example as an enum.

## Exception

NULL genuinely means "not answered yet" and the code treats it as its own state, for example an optional consent flag.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain nullable-boolean`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
